title: Case management for frequent emergency department attenders and death or intensive care admission: a three-site matched case-control study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between case management enrolment and death or intensive care admission within 12 months among frequent emergency department attenders. Design: matched case-control study at three emergency departments with incidence density sampling of four controls per case within site. Exposure: enrolment before the index date from case management files. Results will be written after abstraction.
introduction: Case management reduces visits less than before-after studies suggest, and its effect on hard outcomes is uncertain; the only case-control estimate came from one site and was imprecise.
methods: Cases and controls were drawn from all three sites, with controls matched within site on age band, sex and calendar month. Conditional logistic regression adjusted for complexity. The single-site plan was withdrawn after the sample size calculation showed it was underpowered.
results: No data have been abstracted yet. The report will present matched sets by site, exposure distributions, the adjusted odds ratio and site-specific estimates.
discussion: The discussion will weigh the estimate against confounding by indication and site differences.
limitations: Residual confounding; exposure read from files of varying completeness; fewer community cases.
summary: STROBE-structured draft; the methods record the withdrawn single-site plan.
